abstract: |
  NuSEDS (New Salmon Escapement Database System) estimate Types 1--6 are used throughout the Pacific Region as a concise indicator of how interpretable a spawner abundance estimate is for downstream uses (e.g., stock assessment and Wild Salmon Policy status workflows). In practice, Type assignment has varied across programs because historical guidance does not explicitly address several common complications such as incomplete run-window coverage, outages and missed observation, breach/bypass at counting sites, visibility constraints, and incomplete documentation. This technical report updates the Type 1--6 guidance by operationalizing the intent of Kim Hyatt's 1997 classification key as a property-first decision sequence. The updated key separates enumeration (field) methods from estimation (analysis) methods, defines method families, and records standardized qualifier codes that document why an estimate was conservatively downgraded (for example because of timing, coverage/uptime, breach/bypass, visibility, documentation, or quantified uncertainty such as CV/SE). The report also identifies a minimal set of metadata elements needed for interpretable Type assignment in NuSEDS, with an emphasis on Stream Escapement Narratives (SENs) and controlled vocabularies for downgrade criteria and uncertainty metrics. Adoption of this guidance is expected to improve cross-program consistency, increase transparency of classification decisions, and support more defensible downstream use of escapement estimates.

csas_kable <- function(x,
                       caption = NULL,
                       align = NULL,
                       ...) {
  align_kable <- align
  if (!is.null(align) && length(align) > 1) {
    align_kable <- paste0(align, collapse = "")
  }

  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    csasdown::csas_table(
      x,
      format = "latex",
      caption = caption,
      align = align,
      ...
    )
  } else if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
    knitr::kable(
      x,
      format = "html",
      caption = caption,
      align = align_kable,
      escape = TRUE
    ) |>
      kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
  } else {
    knitr::kable(
      x,
      caption = caption,
      align = align_kable,
      escape = TRUE
    )
  }
}

# Apply column width styling only for HTML/LaTeX outputs.
# For docx/officedown, keep tables plain to avoid HTML widget leakage.
csas_colspec <- function(tbl, column, width) {
  if (knitr::is_html_output() || knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    kableExtra::column_spec(tbl, column, width = width)
  } else {
    tbl
  }
}
